summary: Irreducible self-crossing has no greatest C/D minorant; exact canonical error is ceil(3m/2)/m−1.
detailedSummary: Proves domain normalization, exact conductor/quotients, signed primary obstacle, complete raw envelope and every-degree canonical ideals over characteristic-not-two fields in every dimension at least two, and excellent DVR surfaces with two invertible. Every competitor has actual ample primary positivity before limits. This is a nonnormal failure, not a normal CE counterexample.
text:
Use ENTIRE qualified G331 and n1--n2. For ANY field k with char(k)!=2 and d>=2, let z=(z_1,...,z_(d-1)) and R=k[u,v,z]_(u,v,z)/(v^2-u^2(1+u)), m=(u,v,z). This is an excellent DOMAIN of dimension d: 1+u is not a square in k(u,z), since its prime divisor has odd order, so the quadratic is irreducible. Its parametrization is u=t^2-1, v=t(t^2-1). The normal polynomial ring S_0=k[t,z] is finite over unlocalized R_0 via integral t satisfying t^2=1+u, and has the same fraction field because t=v/u. It is the normalization. Localizing by R_0\m gives a NORMAL DOMAIN S with exactly two centres M_+=(t-1,z), M_-=(t+1,z). It equals the semilocalization of k[t,z] at those centres: an element outside their union is a unit in the finite algebra over local R. S is not a product.

The conductor is exact. With A=k[u,z], S_0=A direct-sum tA and R_0=A direct-sum tuA. Membership of a+t b in R_0 requires b divisible by u; multiplication by t additionally requires a divisible by u. Conversely uS_0 multiplies S_0 into R_0. Thus the conductor is uS_0 before localization and uS afterwards, by localization of the annihilator of finite S_0/R_0. As an R-ideal it is (u,v). Its quotients are R/c=k[z]_(z) and S/c=TWO copies of that ring, using coprime factors t-1,t+1. Exactly R=k[z]_(z)+uS, by subtracting the lifted quotient residue. This is a conductor fibre product, not a decomposition of the normalization domain. Moreover mS=(u,z), which is the maximal ideal on each normal local centre because the opposite sign factor is a unit.

Every finite-u target boundary point has its unique source lift. At infinite u-value, EVERY quotient-boundary semivaluation on k[z] has two lifts, one on each centre, and precisely these are identified by G331. For d=2 the conductor boundary is one point o with z_1=1; in higher dimension every quotient support remains. This proves the marked-centre hypothesis of n2 for an irreducible germ.

There is an explicit obstacle independent of an unknown Izumi constant. Let ell=v-u=u(t-1), I=(ell)+m^2 and F=(1/2)v(I)-2v(m). This is a continuous signed ACTUAL primary-model evaluation. At the plus centre put s=w(t-1), Z=min_j w(z_j); min(s,Z)=1 and w(u)=s, while t+1 is a unit. Hence w(ell)=2s>=2 and F=-1 on the ENTIRE plus boundary. At the minus centre put r=w(t+1); min(r,Z)=1, t-1 is a unit and w(ell)=r. Thus F=(1/2)min(r,2)-2, in [-3/2,-1]. Every conductor value is -1. Infinite coordinates are included; I is proper primary.

The generic ordinary-order valuation nu_- of the regular minus centre has r=Z=1 and F=-3/2. Every normalized semivaluation on that centre dominates ordinary order: all regular parameters have value>=1, elements of the e-th maximal power have value>=e, and units have value0. Hence w(J)>=nu_-(J) for every target unit-or-primary ideal. Negative REAL combinations, G331 uniform comparison and actual decreasing infima give g(rho w)<=g(rho nu_-) for EVERY target geometric C/D function on the entire minus image, including conductor supports. All minorants of F are therefore <=-3/2 there.

For n>=1 let j_n=u(t+1)^(n-1), an ACTUAL R-element by the conductor, T_n=m^(3n)+(j_n)m^(2n), and q_n=-v(T_n)/(2n). On the plus centre, q_n=max(-3/2,-1-s/(2n)); on the minus centre, w(j_n)=nr>=n and q_n=-3/2. These are <=F on every source/target support. Their negative effective primary divisors -E_(T_n)/(2n) are relatively ample and positive on EVERY contracted integral curve before limits. The constant -3/2 is also a competitor. Therefore the COMPLETE raw C/D supremum is p=-1 on the plus-centre finite-u locus and p=-3/2 on the entire minus image, including every conductor point.

At the plus centre, monomial w_R(t-1)=R and w_R(z_j)=1 converge pointwise as R->infinity to the valuation killing t-1 with ordinary z-order. Every fixed local unit denominator has value0. Target restrictions converge to a conductor point where p drops by1/2. Thus p is not USC and no greatest C or D minorant exists. This is NONNORMAL failure on an irreducible germ, not normal CE failure. Its USC regularization has value -1 at that conductor point and -3/2 at nu_-: the open test v(ell)<2 near nu_- meets only the minus image. These values violate g(o)<=g(nu_-), so regularization does not restore geometric positivity.

The canonical ideals are explicit in EVERY degree. Put c_m=ceil(3m/2) and, in S, J_m=(t-1,z)^(m-1)(t+1,z)^(c_m-1). The two semilocal ideals are comaximal because2 is invertible, so their product equals their intersection. Then A_m(F)=(z)^(c_m)R+uJ_m. This is a genuine R-ideal. Explicit finite generators are the z-monomials of total degree c_m and u t^epsilon times every product of a degree-(m-1) monomial in (t-1,z) and a degree-(c_m-1) monomial in (t+1,z), for epsilon=0,1. S=R+Rt, so these generate uJ_m over R. They are actual downstairs polynomials; use t^2=1+u and ut=v to express them in u,v,z.

Proof: ordinary-order tests at the plus/minus centres force respectively order>=m and order>=c_m. These suffice on EVERY source support by domination of ordinary order and F=-1 or F>=-3/2. Write f=g(z)+u a, with g in the local z-ring and a in S. The minus order condition forces g in (z)^(c_m), by reduction modulo the regular parameter u. Subtract the residue lift. Since u is a regular parameter at BOTH centres, the remaining u a has the required orders exactly when a lies in the (m-1)-st plus power and (c_m-1)-st minus power after localization. In the semilocal ring these are the intersection J_m. The converse is immediate. This includes localized denominators and cancellation and proves the ideal identity rather than inferring it from samples.

Localization at the plus centre makes the other centre's power unit. Hence on EVERY plus support, h_m=-min(c_m Z,s+m-1)/m. On every minus support and conductor point, h_m=-c_m/m. Every h_m has actual negative effective ample primary positivity from n1. These formulas prove pointwise convergence to p in EVERY degree. The EXACT uniform error is ||p-h_m||=c_m/m-1>=1/2: on the plus finite-u locus it is at most this number and is attained at Z=1 and finite s>=c_m-m+1; on the minus image the gap is c_m/m-3/2. Thus even degrees have error1/2, odd degrees have error1/2+1/(2m). The canonical algebra is not finitely generated by n1. Uniform perturbations <1/4 preserve failure using q_n-epsilon and the same ordinary-order inequality.

The proof already works in every field dimension d>=2 with char(k)!=2. It also works on the genuinely mixed-characteristic irreducible SURFACE R=V[u,v]_(pi,u,v)/(v^2-u^2(1+u)), for any excellent DVR V with2 invertible. The normalization is the semilocal DOMAIN V[t] at (pi,t-1),(pi,t+1), conductor uS, quotient V downstairs and V times V upstairs, and mS=(pi,u). The same rank-two module calculation proves normalization and conductor; irreducibility follows over Frac(V)(u), and V[t] is regular/normal. Replace z by pi throughout. Ordinary (pi,t+1)-order is a valuation because its associated graded ring is a polynomial domain, and every normalized support dominates it. The same F,T_n,A_m,h_m,p and exact gap formulas hold. No claim is made when2 is not invertible; the characteristic-two displayed field equation is not an automatic transfer.

All expressions are homogeneous. Transporting the obstacle to another primary gauge leaves canonical ideals unchanged and divides profiles and p by the bounded positive gauge factor. Greatest-minorant failure is gauge invariant. Completion transport holds, although irreducible nonnormal R need not have a domain completion. No analytic irreducibility is asserted for R. Literal radial comparison, products, energy and full operators remain separate. Artifacts n3.md, n3.tex and reports/diagnostics.json. Rerun: python diagnostics.py; python assemble.py; python verify_delivery.py. Finite checks are observations; the argument above proves the all-support formulas.
